summary:
Implemented the window title feature in the repository, but nothing was run. Per your instructions I did not run tests or repository code, so all changes are verified only by reading.

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 as the last ControlType member; widened ControlCode with Tuple[ControlType, str].
- rich/control.py: added the format entry "\x1b]0;{title}\x07" and Control.title(title), which passes the control as one two-item tuple.
- rich/console.py: added set_window_title(title) -> bool beside show_cursor. It checks only is_terminal, writes the control and returns True, or returns False with nothing written. Docstring includes the Rich-cannot-restore caveat.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: one new elif branch that calls term.set_title(title) with the title text.
- CHANGELOG.md: new Unreleased "Added" section above "Fixed" with a bullet linking PR 2200.
- Tests: test_console.py (set_window_title writes the sequence and returns True; assertions skipped on legacy Windows), test_control.py (Control.title segment check), test_windows_renderer.py (set_title called once with "Hello, world!").

Choices I made: the Console test uses an if-guard on legacy_windows rather than pytest.skip; set_window_title does not use the dumb-terminal guard that control() applies, since the spec says to check only the terminal check. Nothing was committed.
